reasons: The comment says nothing is guessed, but the Africa split defaults to Middle East.
No tests are visible in this packet.
Adding a new view needs changes in several places.

terms.meaning: A named group that a project is placed into, such as Europe or Cancelled.
A compact text rule that checks whether words appear in a piece of text.
A fixed set of colours chosen for a design.
A label that tells the code what shape of value to expect.

sections.name: File setup, BubbleDimensionKey
sections.title: Imports and the three view names
sections.what: Brings in the colour set and the region lookup, and defines the three view names: region, segment and status.
sections.why: The header comment states that all colours come from the shared colour file, so the chart's colours stay consistent with the rest of the deck.

sections.name: HouseRegion
sections.title: House region names
sections.what: Lists the seven region names used in the house deck, including Other for anything unmapped. Middle East and Africa are kept separate, and Asia and Oceania are combined as Asia-Pacific.
sections.why: The comment says these names follow the house master deck, not the app's own region names.
sections.watch_out: These names differ from the region names in regions.ts, so a conversion step is needed between them.

sections.name: AFRICA_COUNTRIES
sections.title: Short list of African countries
sections.what: A small set of African country names and codes, used only to decide whether a Middle East and Africa project is shown as Africa or Middle East.
sections.why: The region lookup does not separate these two areas, so this list does it by hand.
sections.watch_out: Any African country missing from this list is labelled Middle East, so the list needs regular checking.

sections.name: houseRegionForCountry
sections.title: Turning a country into a house region
sections.what: Looks up the country's region in the main lookup. Then North America, Latin America and Europe are kept as they are, Asia and Oceania become Asia-Pacific, Middle East and Africa is split using the African list, and anything else becomes Other.
sections.why: The comments say the house deck groups regions differently from the app's own grouping.
sections.watch_out: A country that the lookup does not recognise becomes Other here, which is separate from the Unknown label used in regions.ts.

sections.name: HOUSE_REGION_ORDER
sections.title: Order of regions in the legend
sections.what: Lists the seven house regions in the order they appear in the chart legend, with Other last.
sections.why: A fixed order makes the legend read the same way every time.
sections.watch_out: This order is separate from the region order in regions.ts, so the two lists can drift apart.

sections.name: HOUSE_REGION_COLORS
sections.title: Colour for each house region
sections.what: Gives each house region a colour, taken from the shared region palette, with Asia-Pacific and Other using their own shared colours.
sections.why: Keeps regions visually distinct and matches the house colours.
sections.watch_out: Whether the palette keys match these region names is not visible in this packet.

sections.name: STATUS_BUCKET_ORDER, StatusBucket
sections.title: Status groups in display order
sections.what: Lists the seven status groups in the order they should appear: Cancelled, Halted or dropped, On hold, Announced or planned, Completed or operational, Under construction, and Other. The type for a status group is built from this list.
sections.why: The comment says the order is deliberate, with terminal outcomes first and announced before completed.
sections.watch_out: Reordering this list also changes the legend order, and the status checks rely on the same order.

sections.name: statusBucket
sections.title: Reading status text into a group
sections.what: Upper-cases and trims the status text, then checks keyword rules in a fixed order: cancelled first, then halted or dropped, then on hold, then announced or planned, then completed or operational, then under construction. Blank or unmatched text becomes Other.
sections.why: Status is free text, so keyword rules give a coarse but explainable grouping.
sections.watch_out: The order matters: text that mentions both announced and operational is grouped as announced. Postponed and suspended projects land in On hold here, but count as Dropped in the appendix table.

sections.name: STATUS_BUCKET_COLORS
sections.title: Colour for each status group
sections.what: Assigns each status group a colour: red for cancelled, dark red for halted or dropped, amber for on hold, grey for announced, green for completed, the palette blue for under construction, and a neutral colour for Other.
sections.why: Gives an at-a-glance meaning: red for failure, green for finished, amber for paused.
sections.watch_out: A new status group needs a colour here, or it will fall back to an automatically chosen one.

sections.name: BubbleDimension
sections.title: Shape of a view definition
sections.what: Describes what each view must provide: a key, a label, a way to get the value from a project, an optional fixed order, and optional fixed colours.
sections.why: A common shape lets the chart treat all views the same way.
sections.watch_out: Views without fixed colours get colours by position, so the same group can change colour when the set of groups on screen changes.

sections.name: BUBBLE_DIMENSIONS
sections.title: The three views defined
sections.what: Defines the region view (from country, with the house order and colours), the segment view (from sub-industry, with unknown values shown as Unspecified and no fixed order), and the status view (from status, with the status order and colours).
sections.why: These are the three ways the bubble chart can colour and filter projects.
sections.watch_out: The segment view has no fixed order, so its groups are sorted alphabetically.

sections.name: bucketsPresent
sections.title: Groups present in the current selection
sections.what: Works out which groups actually appear in the selected projects, in the fixed order first, then any extra groups in alphabetical order.
sections.why: Lets the legend list only what is on screen.

sections.name: colorMapFor
sections.title: Colour map for groups on screen
sections.what: Gives each group on screen its colour: the fixed colour if one exists, otherwise a colour from the shared categorical list in order, starting again from the beginning when the list runs out.
sections.why: Gives every visible group a distinct colour without hand-picking one for every value.
sections.watch_out: When there are more groups than colours, two groups can end up with the same colour, which makes them hard to tell apart.

summary: Defines the three ways the bubble chart can group and colour projects (region, segment and status), with the labels and colours for each group.
purpose: Lets the chart switch between views while keeping group names and colours consistent.
why: The header comment says every group comes from real project values, with unknown countries put in Other and missing segments in Unspecified.
how: 1. Declares the three view names. 2. Maps each project's country to a house region, splitting the Middle East and Africa group with a short list of African countries. 3. Maps each project's status text to one of seven status groups using keyword rules. 4. Lists the three views with how to read each project. 5. Orders the groups and assigns colours, using fixed colours where they exist and a shared palette otherwise. 6. Lists only the groups that actually appear.
inputs: Project records, mainly the country, sub-industry and status fields, plus the shared colours and the region lookup.
outputs: For each project, a group name in each view; an ordered list of the groups present; and a colour for each group.
risks: The African country list is short, so any African country not on it is labelled Middle East. This conflicts with the comment saying nothing is guessed. Status is matched by keyword, so unusual wording falls into Other. Projects with no sub-industry become Unspecified.
debug: If a project shows in the wrong group, check its country or status text against the matching rule. If colours seem to shift between views, check whether that view has fixed colours. If a region is missing, check the country lookup in regions.ts.
